data.builder.columnDropped: Column "{column}" has {count, plural, one {{shown} distinct value} other {{shown} distinct values}}, more than the {max} that can be picked in a filter or a difference split, so it was not retained. If it identifies an entity, map it as the person column; if it is a per-match key, filter by time range instead.
data.builder.groupsDropped: Group column has {count, plural, one {{shown} distinct value} other {{shown} distinct values}}, and at most {max} can be grouped by — every group needs a row in the group list and a texel in the table the shader reads. Loaded without groups. If it identifies an entity, map it as the person column instead; if you want to slice by it, add it as an extra column and filter on it.
data.builder.sharedNames: {shared} of {total, plural, one {# name is} other {# names are}} used by more than one thing at a time ({more, select, yes {{examples}, …} other {{examples}}}) — they report from two places in the same match at the same instant, which one entity cannot do. Usually every AI in every match shares one name. Those names are played back as single samples: no interpolation and no trail, because a line between two of their samples is a line between two different creatures. Everything else is unaffected.
data.builder.sessionsDropped: Session column has {count, plural, one {{shown} distinct value} other {{shown} distinct values}}, and at most {max} can be listed — a picker cannot offer more, and sending that many labels to the viewer is what a browser tab runs out of memory doing. Loaded without a session picker, but the boundaries themselves are kept: nothing is interpolated or trailed across a match boundary, and each row's lifetime still stops at the end of its own match. If it identifies a match, it is one value per match that is wanted here; if you want to slice by it, add it as an extra column and filter on it.
data.ingestFiles.shortUnread: Loaded {loaded} of about {expected, plural, one {# row} other {# rows}} — {missing, plural, one {# is missing} other {# are missing}} ({percent}%). {count, plural, one {# file} other {# files}} could not be read; see below. Anything derived from density is affected.
data.ingestFiles.shortDropped: Loaded {loaded} of about {expected, plural, one {# row} other {# rows}} — {missing, plural, one {# is missing} other {# are missing}} ({percent}%). Rows without a usable position are dropped, which can account for it. Anything derived from density is affected.
data.ingestFiles.stride: {ord, select, one {every {stride}st row} two {every {stride}nd row} few {every {stride}rd row} other {every {stride}th row}}
data.ingest.twoAxes: At least two position columns must be mapped (any two of X / Y / Z). The third is optional and is treated as 0, giving a flat plane.
data.ingest.separator: Separator must be a single character.
data.ingest.allRejected: {count, plural, one {The # row in {file} was rejected} other {All # rows in {file} were rejected}} — check the X/Y/Z mapping.
data.ingest.noIsoTimes: No parseable ISO-8601 timestamps in the mapped time column.
data.ingestParquet.noColumn: {file} has no column "{column}" (mapped as {role, select, x {X} y {Y} z {Z} yaw {yaw} pitch {pitch} dirX {dir X} dirY {dir Y} dirZ {dir Z} time {time} person {person id} team {team id} session {session id} other {filter}}).
data.ingestParquet.noPositions: Every row in {file} has a non-finite position — check the mapping.
data.ocap.notOcap: {file} is not an OCAP recording of an Arma mission: it has no entities and no capture delay.
data.csv.tooManyFields: Row has more than {max} fields — is the delimiter right?
data.sort.tooMany: Cannot sort {count, plural, one {{rows} row} other {{rows} rows}} in time order in the browser. Load fewer rows (every Nth row, as the fit check offers, or fewer files), or unmap the time column: without it the rows keep their file order and are never sorted.
data.synth.name: Synthetic
data.classify.singleMesh: single unnamed mesh — treated as ground
data.classify.navigation: navigation mesh — not drawn, as it lies on the ground; clicks still find it
data.modelWorker.packing: Packing {count, plural, one {# texture} other {# textures}}
data.modelWorker.classifying: Classifying {count, plural, one {# part} other {# parts}}
data.modelWorker.simplifyingGround: Simplifying ground ({count, plural, one {# tri} other {# tris}})
data.modelWorker.simplifyingStructures: Simplifying structures ({count, plural, one {# tri} other {# tris}})
data.modelParse.glbTooShort: File is too short to be a GLB.
data.modelParse.externalBuffer: glTF references an external buffer. Export as a single .glb so the geometry is embedded.
data.modelParse.binaryPly: Only ASCII PLY is supported. Convert to .glb or binary .stl.
data.simplify.unavailable: The mesh simplifier is unavailable in this browser (WebAssembly required).
data.validate.noAxes: Map at least two position columns. Any two of X / Y / Z will do — the data is then drawn as a plane in the 3D scene.
data.validate.oneAxis: Only {axis} is mapped. At least two position axes are needed; any pair of X / Y / Z works.
data.validate.plane: Drawing on the {plane} plane — {flat} is unmapped and treated as 0, so everything is flat.
data.validate.sameColumn: The same column is mapped to more than one position axis, which collapses the data onto a line.
data.validate.notInFile: Column "{column}" (mapped as {role, select, x {X} y {Y} z {Z} time {time} person {person id} group {group} yaw {yaw} other {pitch}}) is not in this file.
data.validate.notNumeric: "{column}" (mapped as {axis}) does not look numeric — every row would be rejected.
data.validate.groupLooksLikeId: "{column}" (mapped as group) takes {count, plural, one {# distinct value} other {# distinct values}} across {rows, plural, one {# sampled row} other {# sampled rows}}, so it looks like an id rather than a group. Above {max} distinct values the load keeps every row but drops the grouping. Map it as the person column if it identifies an entity.
data.validate.dateColumn: "{column}" is a DATE column, so every row in a day shares one instant. Playback will jump a day at a time. Look for an event-time or duration column instead.
data.validate.timeNotNumeric: "{column}" is not numeric. Set the time unit to ISO-8601 if it holds timestamp strings.
data.validate.noTime: No time column mapped, so the timeline is unavailable — the view stays in All mode showing every datapoint.
data.validate.noPerson: No person column mapped. Tracks, interpolation, trails and per-datapoint lifetime all need one.
data.validate.lifetimeNeedsTime: Lifetime needs a time column as well as a person column.
data.validate.noGroup: No group column mapped, so everything shares one colour, and difference mode can only split on a column kept for filtering.
data.validate.noYaw: Look direction is set to yaw/pitch but no yaw column is chosen.
data.validate.noVector: Look direction is set to a vector but not all three components are chosen.
data.validate.zeroScale: Unit scale is 0, which would collapse everything to the origin.
data.validate.blocked.oneGroup: Difference mode needs two groups or a column kept for filtering to split on; this data has one group.
data.validate.blocked.noGroup: Difference mode needs a group column or a column kept for filtering to split on.
data.validate.blocked.teams: Teams mode colours the heat by group; this data has no group column.
data.validate.blocked.team: Team view needs a person column to build tracks from.
data.validate.blocked.lines: Line heat needs a person column and a time column, to know whose samples follow whose.
data.memory.ram.host: {total} installed and {free} free (reported by the dev server, not the browser); {basis, select, free {{percent}% of free} other {{percent}% of installed}} budgeted
data.memory.ram.hostTotal: {total} installed (reported by the dev server, not the browser); {percent}% budgeted
data.memory.ram.deviceCapped: {gib}GiB installed or more (most browsers clamp this figure at 8), {percent}% budgeted
data.memory.ram.tabCap: capped at {max}, the most one tab can allocate
data.memory.gpu.default: no VRAM API exists; conservative default
data.memory.gpu.discrete: no VRAM API exists; {px}px max texture suggests a discrete GPU
data.memory.gpu.modest: no VRAM API exists; {px}px max texture suggests a modest GPU
data.memory.gpu.buffer: no VRAM API exists; {buffer} max buffer suggests at least {total}
data.memory.cpu.cores: {count, plural, one {# logical core reported} other {# logical cores reported}}
data.memory.note.gpu: No API reports how much memory a GPU has, so that ceiling is inferred rather than measured — {source}. A card with more than {max} is common; raise it under Resource budgets if this one has it.
data.memory.note.capped: That budget is 60% of the 8GiB Chrome and Edge report as installed, which is all they will say — a machine with more RAM reports the same 8. Raise it under Resource budgets if this one does.
data.memory.note.busyHeld: That budget is set by how much memory is free right now — {total} installed, but {used} of it is in use, not by this machine's capacity. Closing other programs and pressing Re-detect under Resource budgets raises it, up to {ceiling}.
data.memory.note.busy: That budget is set by how much memory is free right now, not by this machine's capacity. Closing other programs and pressing Re-detect under Resource budgets raises it, up to {ceiling}.
data.memory.fit.stride: {ord, select, one {Loading every {stride}st row fits} two {Loading every {stride}nd row fits} few {Loading every {stride}rd row fits} other {Loading every {stride}th row fits}} (~{rows, plural, one {# row} other {# rows}}) and gives the same heat distribution with more noise.
data.memory.fit.pastSort: {rows, plural, one {# row is} other {# rows is}} past the {max} that can be put in time order in a browser tab. Memory is not the constraint here — this selection needs {needs} and the budget is {budget}.
data.memory.fit.unmapTime: Unmapping the time column also removes the limit, at the cost of the timeline: without it the rows keep their file order and are never sorted.
data.memory.fit.tooBig: {peak} peak RAM and {gpu} of GPU memory for {rows, plural, one {# row} other {# rows}} exceeds the {limit, select, ram {memory} other {GPU}} budget ({budget}).
data.memory.fit.alternatives: Alternatively drop filter columns, unmap the time column, or raise the budget under Resource budgets.
data.memory.fit.nearSort: {rows, plural, one {# row is} other {# rows is}} near the {max} that can be put in time order in a tab. It should load, but putting the rows in time order is a pass over all of them and takes a while with no progress to show for it.
data.memory.fit.tight: {peak} peak RAM is close to the {budget} budget. It should load, but expect it to be slow.
data.filePick.notMovement: not a movement file, and this folder has movement files
data.levelLibrary.openFailed: Could not open the level library.
